# Pinned upstream SPDX corpus

These are unchanged example/test SBOM files from official project repositories,
not files generated by running all tools locally. They represent concrete producer
outputs and interoperability inputs, including one deliberately unsupported
ambiguous input. They do not establish support for every tool version.

[sources.json](sources.json) records the repository, immutable commit, source path,
raw URL and SHA-256 for every file. Tests verify those hashes and use only local
files, so upstream changes and network availability cannot alter test outcomes.
Each original document declares DataLicense: CC0-1.0. The files retain their original
SPDX metadata, attribution and package licensing fields; package licenses describe
the inventoried software, not a relicensing of those packages by Nibmark.

| Fixture                    | Source                                           | Expected outcome with default root selection                                         |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| syft-alpine.json           | Syft SPDX JSON test data                         | 3 packages; no explicit root; Alpine ecosystem fallback                              |
| syft-tag-value.spdx        | Syft Tag/Value test data                         | 4 packages; missing document-name warning; Alpine/Maven fallback                     |
| trivy-bom.json             | Trivy SPDX interoperability test data            | 12 records minus 1 described container = 11; containment never implies dependency    |
| trivy-files.json           | Trivy file-relationship test data                | 3 records minus 1 described root = 2; file entries excluded                          |
| trivy-empty.json           | Trivy root-only test data                        | 1 record minus root = 0; deprecated documentDescribes alias still resolves the root  |
| trivy-no-relationship.json | Third-party Elasticsearch fixture in Trivy tests | Reject document/package SPDX ID collision; do not guess or silently merge identities |
| tern-photon.json           | Tern Photon container example                    | 38 records minus image root = 37; layer/package records remain distinct              |
| tern-photon.spdx           | Tern Photon Tag/Value example                    | Same inventory as JSON; original creation timestamps differ                          |

The default Trivy container root has no dependency edges, so its 11 remaining
packages are unclassified. Choosing its composer application as root yields two
explicit direct dependencies and nine unclassified package records. The tests
assert both cases. Tern lists containment, so it does not imply direct dependencies.

The corpus spans 2.2/2.3 and JSON/Tag-Value. Existing synthetic fixtures continue
to test cycles, duplicate edges, typed relationships, missing fields and bounds.
No fixture content is executed; only the inventory metadata is parsed/rendered.

To update a fixture, deliberately select a new upstream commit, preserve the
original bytes, update its manifest hash and independently review expected counts.
Do not replace the expectations with the importer's observed output automatically.
